figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. The predicted ustilaginoidin synthesis (ugs) gene cluster and the putative catalytic domains in the polyketide synthase UvPKS1 in
U. virens.
A. The ugs gene cluster in U. virens. UvPKS1, ugsZ, ugsT and ugsL were identiﬁed in U. virens by Blast searches against the aurofusarin bio-
synthesis gene cluster in F. graminearum; and ugsR1, ugsR2, ugsS, ugsO and ugsJ were predicted based on the similar structural domains via
Pfam searches. The genes in the ugs cluster labelled in white arrows are absent from the aur gene cluster.
B. The putative structural domains in UvPKS1. UvPKS1 carries the starter ACP transcylase (SAT) domain at the N-terminus, β-ketoacyl synthase
(KS), acyl transferase (AT) and acyl carrier protein (ACP) domains in the middle and thioesterase (TE) domain at the C-terminus.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. The HPLC proﬁles of ustilaginoidin derivatives and intermediates extracted from the wild-type, mutant and complementary strains.
Colony morphologies and HPLC proﬁles of ethyl acetate extracts of the wild-type (WT), ΔUvPKS1 and ΔUvPKS1/UvPKS1 complementary
strains (A); the WT, ΔugsO and ΔugsO/ugsO strains (B); the WT, ΔugsT and ΔugsT/ugsT strains (C); and the WT, ΔugsJ and ΔugsJ/ugsJ
strains (D). Left columns: colony morphologies of different U. virens mutant and complementary strains were observed after 4 weeks of culturing
on the PSA plates; Right columns: the metabolite proﬁles of ethyl acetate extracts from the wild-type, mutant and complementary strains were
detected via HPLC with UV at 290 nm.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. Isolation and identiﬁcation of monomeric intermediates for ustilaginoidin biosynthesis in the ΔugsL mutant.
A. The HPLC proﬁles of ethyl acetate extracts from the wild-type (WT), ΔugsL and complementary ΔugsL/ugsL strains. The three novel peaks
corresponding to the compounds 9, 10 and 11 were detected in ethyl acetate extracts of the ΔugsL mutant, but not in the wild-type strain. The
majority of peaks corresponding to 5 ustilaginoidin derivatives except for ustilaginoidins N (5), O (6) and M (8) were detected in the complemen-
tary strain ΔugsL/ugsL.
B. HR-ESI-MS analysis of the metabolites 9, 10 and 11 from the ΔugsL mutant. The mass to charge ratios (m/z) of compounds 9, 10 and 11 were
determined by LC–MS analysis to be 259.0581, 273.0738 and 273.0742 (= [M-H]−), equivalent to the molecular formula of C14H12O5, C15H14O5
and C15H14O5, respectively.
C. 1H and 13C NMR analytic data for structural identiﬁcation of the compound 11.
D. The selected HMBC correlations from protons to carbons in the compound 11. Based on these data, the compound 11 was determined to be
3-methyl-dihydro-nor-rubrofusarin. The three compounds are most likely to be the monomeric intermediates for ustilaginoidin biosynthesis.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. The proposed model for the ustilaginoidin biosynthetic pathway.
Nor-rubrofusarin (a) is synthesized as a primary product from one molecule of acetyl-CoA and six molecules of malonyl-CoA under the catalyza-
tion of the polyketide synthase UvPKS1. Nor-rubrofusarin can be readily hydrogenated to generate dihydro-nor-rubrofusarin (b), which is then
subject to UgsJ-mediated methylation to form 3-methyl-dihydro-nor-rubrofusarin (c). Subsequently, the methylated and nonmethylated heptake-
tide derivatives are subjected to UgsL-catalysed oxidation and dimerization to generate different ustilaginoidin derivatives. Besides, some ustilagi-
noidin derivatives are further modiﬁed. For example, ustilaginoidins N (5), O (6) and M (8) are reversibly reduced to ustilaginoidins E (4) and
D (7), which is catalysed by UgsO.
